comments.note: Toggle: IObfuscationService.ToggleAsync contract explicitly states it does NOT throw OperationCanceledException. The catch in ObfuscationSettingsViewModel is purely defensive — correct and harmless. Any non-OCE exception from ToggleAsync would propagate through AsyncRelayCommand (generated by [RelayCommand]), which by default does not surface to the UI unless explicitly bound. This is acceptable given no error reporting AC exists for ToggleAsync failures.

comments.note: IObfuscationService.ToggleAsync — the `bool enable` parameter was added by this WP to fix a WP-003 omission. No concrete implementors exist yet (WP-008 will add one), so there are no downstream breakages. Confirmed: zero build errors, zero warnings. The interface XML doc is excellent — it explicitly documents the no-OperationCanceledException contract, making caller intent clear.

ObfuscationSettingsViewModel.Toggle: `var target = !IsEnabled` is computed before the await, correctly capturing the toggle target before any async suspension. This prevents a subtle race condition where IsEnabled could change on the UI thread between the await and the IsEnabled assignment post-completion. Excellent pattern.

ObfuscationSettingsViewModel.Toggle: Progress string is set to 'Starting…' at entry and only updated to 'Idle' inside the try block on success. If ToggleAsync throws a non-OCE exception (which the interface contract says it won't), Progress remains 'Starting…' after IsBusy resets to false — giving a misleading UI state. A catch-all or a `Progress = "Error"` in the finally block would improve resilience. Not blocking given the explicit no-throw contract.

ObfuscationSettingsViewModel: `IsBusy = true` is set slightly outside the try block. The code between the assignment and the try block (Errors.Clear, Progress assignment, variable init) is trivially safe, so the risk of IsBusy becoming stuck is negligible. The pattern is consistent with common async ViewModels. No change required.
